title: Retrospective studies on cirrhotic and non-cirrhotic portal hypertension
summary:
Background
So-called portal hypertension occurs when blood flow through the liver is obstructed. This blockage can occur before the liver, within the liver itself, or after the liver. The most common cause is liver cirrhosis, a scarring and remodeling disease of the liver, which accounts for more than 80% of cases.
Portal hypertension can lead to severe complications. These include, among others, varicose veins in the esophagus (esophageal varices), which may cause life-threatening bleeding, accumulation of fluid in the abdomen (ascites), bacterial infections within the abdominal cavity, and kidney failure as part of advanced liver disease.
For many of these complications, established treatment standards already exist, such as medication to prevent bleeding or endoscopic procedures to treat high-risk varices in the esophagus. Nevertheless, the disease and its consequences often remain severe. For example, bleeding from esophageal varices is still associated with high mortality despite treatment. This highlights the need for further improvement of current therapeutic strategies. In the Department of Liver Fibrosis and Portal Hypertension at the Medical Clinic I of the University Hospital Bonn, many affected patients are treated. A major focus is the management of severe cases by creating a artificial blood-vessel within the liver to lower the pressure within portal vein. In addition, the working group has been conducting extensive scientific research on these diseases for many years.

Research Question
The aim of the planned analysis is to retrospectively evaluate existing clinical data from patients with portal hypertension.
The study will investigate whether there are differences between cirrhotic (caused by liver cirrhosis) and non-cirrhotic forms of the disease, and identify potential factors that influence disease progression—for example, which patients have a higher risk of complications, hospital admissions, or increased mortality.
In the long term, the results are intended to improve treatment, follow-up care and to help design future prospective (forward-looking) studies.

Methodology
This is a retrospective study, meaning that already existing medical data are analyzed. Patient treatment is not affected by this analysis.
After inclusion in the study, the data are pseudonymized. This means that personal identifiers are replaced by a study code, so that the data can no longer be directly linked to an individual.
Clinical data, laboratory values, imaging results, and other diagnostic findings will be analyzed. The evaluation is performed using specialized statistical software.
The results of the analysis will not allow any conclusions to be drawn about individual patients. No additional risks or disadvantages arise for the individuals concerned.
The study is conducted in accordance with the principles of Good Clinical Practice and the Declaration of Helsinki. All applicable data protection regulations are strictly observed.

interventions.name: Retrospective analysis of prognostic markers in patients with cirrhotic and non-cirrhotic portal hypertension between 2009 and 2026
